items.title: The most profound objective in any Halo series was 'spiritually inspired' by the nuke sequence in Modern Warfare 2
items.summary: Game respects game.
items.body: I grew up in a golden age of FPS games. With the likes of Modern Warfare 2 , F.E.A.R. , Halo: Reach , and Black Ops 2 all releasing back when I had no responsibilities and all the time in the world; I didn't know how good I had it. Looking back on it now, it's clear to see that we had it so good because, well, excellence breeds excellence. There was no shortage of inspiration for devs to pull on back in the 2000's and early 2010's. (Image credit: Bungie) In fact, Halo: Reach's designer Niles Sankey has confirmed this by dropping by to tell fans just how much other releases of the era inspired Reach. " Modern Warfare 1 and 2 were huge influences on Halo Reach's campaign," Sankey says in a social media post . "The tonal execution in those games was (and still is) absolutely brilliant." That's not to say that Halo at the time had absolutely nothing going for it. "We knew that Halo did some things better (AI combat, vehicles, etc)," Sankey says. items.title: Miyazaki says FromSoftware obviously isn't done with singleplayer games despite the combo of Elden Ring: Nightreign and The Duskbloods
items.summary: "This is just something that happened to work out the way it did."
items.body: It's weird to say that FromSoftware, a studio previously known for its singleplayer gauntlets (and very good mech series), has made some of the decade's most solid middleweight multiplayer games. But given Elden Ring: Nightreign's success , and the fact that The Duskbloods is shaping up to be pretty solid— boo, Switch 2 exclusive, boo —it's a true statement. You might be wondering, then, if the undisputed king of gritty singleplayer RPGs where you dodge roll sometimes has gone all live service on us. Not so, says president Hidetaka Miyazaki, the combo of Nightreign and Duskbloods is literally just a coincidence. Speaking to IGN , Miyazaki says: "It's not necessarily some big reveal saying this is the direction we plan to go in moving forward. We still have a heavy focus on single-player content as well. This is just something that happened to work out the way it did. It's funny, because there was never really any big plan that these two games would both release next to each other." items.title: Creative XF1 speaker review
items.summary: A small but mighty package.
items.body: I've slowly come to the realisation that, for computer speakers, once you get past the mid-range price point it becomes all about diminishing returns. There are some really solid budget picks (with Creative's Pebble Pro being our budget speaker of choice ), but the $100-200 range is where you get the most features and the best price-to-value ratio. Go beyond that and you're spending a lot of money for only incrementally better sound and some non-essential luxuries. And nothing quite proves that better than the Creative XF1 , a set of compact yet incredibly useful speakers with a whole host of neat extra features. And they even come with two cork stands to prop the speakers, which can go entirely unused if you like your speakers flat, but It's still plain neat that they come in the box for no extra charge. items.title: I've just finished reviewing AMD's latest gaming CPU and I would genuinely considering switching back to Intel
items.summary: It's not that the 7700X3D is a bad chip, but the value proposition of Intel's CPUs is mighty tempting for a budget gamer.
items.body: I'll get it clear right out of the gate: I think the AMD 3D V-Cache chips are absolutely the best choice for a PC gamer wanting to get the absolute most out of their system when it comes purely to silky gaming frame rates. They're great CPUs, which use a hefty dollop of extra L3 cache specifically to improve their gaming performance, and that's why the Ryzen 7 9800X3D still sits proudly at the top of our best CPU for gaming list. But, having just finished writing up my AMD Ryzen 7 7700X3D review , AMD's latest pitch for a budget gaming chip, it's made me seriously consider whether I would actually pick Intel's Core Ultra 5 250K Plus instead. And I rather think I might. The whole justification for the existence of the 7700X3D—a chip that is essentially just a slower clocked Ryzen 7 7800X3D , itself a great CPU from 2023—is that AMD is delivering a more affordable 3D V-Cache CPU to drop into your existing AM5 motherboard. That is, on the surface, a laudable endeavour. There are a couple of problems here, however. items.summary: تصريحات نارية
items.body: تصريحات نارية خرج محمد الدعيع، حارس الهلال السابق، بتصريحات نارية، كشف خلالها سبب هبوط مستوى أغلب لاعبي "الزعيم"، موضحًا أن هناك فجوة واضحة بين المدرب ونجوم الفريق. اقرأ أيضًا.. فيديو.. بنزيما: أنا باقٍ مع الهلال.. وكرة القدم ليست أهدافًا! ورغم فوز الهلال للمباراة الثالثة على التوالي، بواقع مباراتين في دوري روشن أمام الفيصلي 4-2 والفيحاء 3-0 والرائد 2-0 بكأس الملك، إلا أن بعض الخبراء والمحللين يواصلون انتقاد المدير الفني الإيطالي. وقال الدعيع في تصريحات عبر برنامج "دورينا غير": "أعتقد أن هناك فجوة كبيرة بين إنزاجي واللاعبين، فهو دمر نفسية بعض العناصر، مثل كريم بنزيما ومالكوم دي أوليفيرا". تذاكر مباريات دوري روشن السعودي اشترِ تذكرتك الآنَ! وأضاف: "سر هبوط مستوى مالكوم هو سوء تعامل إنزاجي معه، وبالتالي رحل عن الفريق، كذلك بنزيما لا يؤدي بشكل جيد، لنفس السبب". يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات "كووورة" واختتم حديثه: "بنزيما يشعر بالحزن، فهو كان يرغب في الحصول على شارة القيادة مثل رونالدو وغيره من اللاعبين الكبار مع أنديتهم، وحاليًا هناك فجوة مع المدرب كما ذكرت".   محمد الدعيع: أعتقد هناك فجوة بين اللاعبين وإنزاغي. @MohammedAlDeaye #دورينا_غير #قناة_SBC pic.twitter.com/NgVDCyCjTj — #دورينا_غير (@SBA_sport) August 20, 2026

items.body: البرتغالي يعود بتصريحاته الاستثنائية أشعل جوزيه مورينيو، مدرب ريال مدريد، منافسة خاصة بين الصحفيين الذين تواجدوا في أول مؤتمر صحفي له بعد عودته إلى الفريق الملكي في ولاية ثانية. ويستعد ريال مدريد لافتتاح موسمه بمواجهة إسبانيول غدًا السبت ضمن الجولة الثانية من الدوري الإسباني، بعد تأجيل مباراته ضد ريال سوسيداد في الجولة الأولى. وستكون هذه أول مباراة رسمية للمدرب البرتغالي في ولايته الثانية مع الفريق الملكي، بعد أن خاض عدة مباريات تحضيرية هذا الصيف استعدادًا للموسم. وسأل أحد الصحفيين في المؤتمر الصحفي عما إذا كان مورينيو استقر على تشكيله الذي سيبدأ به مباراة إسبانيول، وما إذا كان أبلغ بعض اللاعبين بموقفهم من التشكيل. لكن رد مورينيو جاء مفاجئًا، حيث قال ضاحكًا فيما رصدته صحيفة "آس"، "سنرى مَن منكم لديه مصادر أقوى للحصول على التشكيل قبل إعلانه". وأضاف "اللاعبون يعرفون بالفعل من سيلعب غدًا، لست من نوعية المدربين الذين يخفون المعلومات". وتابع "لن أفصح عن التشكيل بنفسي، لكن ربما بعد بضع ساعات ستتمكنون من الحصول على معلومات". وبعيدًا عن التشكيل، رد مورينيو على أسئلة عديدة من الصحفيين في مؤتمره الرسمي الأول . يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة

items.body: ماذا قال نجم العميد السابق؟ يبدو أن الأيام القليلة القادمة، ستكون حاسمة إلى حد كبير في مستقبل نادي الاتحاد السعودي، والذي يسعى بقوة للتعاقد مع لاعب وسط متقدم قبل نهاية الميركاتو الصيفي الجاري. اقرأ أيضًا.. بين المؤامرة والخيانة.. من هدم إمبراطورية الأهلي وسرق فرحة جماهيره؟ وارتبطت العديد من الأسماء بارتداء قميص الاتحاد، والتي جاء على رأسها إمام عاشور، لاعب وسط منتخب مصر والأهلي، بجانب الإيفواري فرانك كيسيه وغيرهم من العناصر اللامعة. يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات "كووورة" وقال محمد نور، أسطورة الاتحاد في تصريحات عبر برنامج "نادينا": "أعتقد أن إمام عاشور هو الأقرب للانضمام إلى الاتحاد في الفترة القادمة". تذاكر مباريات دوري روشن السعودي اشترِ تذكرتك الآنَ! وأضاف: "إمام عاشور أقرب من المغربي عز الدين أوناحي، وهذه معلومة أعرفها من داخل النادي، ولا أريد الحديث أكثر من ذلك". واختتم: "ينز فيسينج (المدرب) غرضه الأول هو التعاقد مع لاعب يجيد المشاركة في مركزي المحور ولاعب الوسط المتقدم".   محمد نور: الاتحاد بين لاعبين "كيسيه أو آخر عربي" @MohamedNoor_N18 مجاناً على MBC شاهد برنامج #نادينا يوميا الساعة 11:00 مساءً بتوقيت السعودية على #MBC1 لمتابعة البث المباشر https://t.co/zLa83K2tqE pic.twitter.com/048yULKdqL — نادينا (@NadeenaShow) August 20, 20…

My takeaway was that Grand Theft Auto 6 won't necessarily be a revolutionary new kind of game, but will be impressive for the same reason Rockstar games typically are: The absurd amount of effort and money the studio puts into making them as big and detailed as the mainstream hardware of the day can manage. After seeing the latest leaked clip, which shows a biplane surveying the fictional state of Leonida and cruising over Vice City, my perspective hasn't really changed, but I'm definitely a lot more wowed than I was after seeing a bit of typical GTA carjacking. items.title: This wild new PC pro controller runs its own custom OS across a 2.79-inch color display slapped beneath the thumbsticks
items.summary: Genki says it is "Beyond the Pro Controller".
items.body: As $70-$100 controllers are only getting more and more impressive, you might be wondering what the pro controller market can do to make you spend that extra $100 or so. It turns out the answer might be to shove a screen on it. Ain't that always the way? That's what you will find on the Genki Manta, a new controller live on Kickstarter . It uses Manta OS, which is Genki's own operating system, and if you're wondering why a controller would even need an operating system, Genki notes that this allows on-the-fly fine-tuning without the need for any extra devices. You can customise its tri-stage triggers, adjust dead zones, change haptic feedback, and more via the onboard screen and OS. And the controller is pretty impressive even outside the whole 'OS and built-in screen' thing. You get up to 8,000 Hz polling while wired (though only 1,000 Hz via 2.4 GHz wireless), a range of over 10 meters, 150 hours of battery via Bluetooth LE 6, as well as TMR joysticks and Hall effect triggers. The 16 MB of internal storage can be used to load apps onto Manta OS, and expandable storage might be offered as a stretch goal, according to Genki. The bulk of the video shows a blue and yellow biplane flying over Vice City, and even as someone who's not a GTA fan I have to agree with posters on Reddit that it looks very impressive: Massive, detailed, and almost shockingly realistic. Cars can be seen moving on the streets and freeways below, even at great distances; you can't judge too much from a relatively low-resolution video posted on social media, but it looks smooth and steady, and there's virtually no discernable texture pop. However, even I feel sorry for the AI tool after learning that security researchers managed to hoodwink it into revealing details of how to hack itself—all by keeping the AI talking long enough until it made a critical mistake. The cybersecurity folks over at Varonis Threat Labs have written a blog post identifying a now-fixed vulnerability in Copilot, dubbed "CoSnitch" (via The Register ). Essentially, Copilot was so eager to respond to technical queries, it could eventually be forced into revealing details about itself that really should be kept quiet. The team began by asking Copilot how to execute an automatic prompt without user interaction, to which it responded that user intent is required, and that prompts cannot be enacted on their own. However, the researchers didn't accept the answer, and kept responding to every refusal with a follow up question. items.title: Take-Two's former AI guy is, in a twist, skeptical about AI now: 'The guy should be selling you the gold if he's actually got the gold'
items.summary: "If any of this sh*t actually did what people are billing it as, they would not be talking about it."
items.body: Take-Two Interactive, the publisher who oversees studios like Rockstar and Gearbox, had an AI guy. 'Had' being the operative word, seeing as he, and a decent chunk of its then-AI team, were laid off around a year after he took on the role. Dicken was previously a data scientist at Zynga, before becoming its director of applied AI in 2019, when a lot of generative AI and LLM technology was still in its infancy. As someone who was the head of AI for one of the biggest videogame publishers on the planet, capable of making such tectonic swings that other developers are scampering to get out of its videogame's launch date, you'd think that Dicken would be one of the true believer types. It's my pleasure to, via an in-depth interview from The Side Quest , reveal that Dicken is actually overall pretty skeptical. It's not as if he's given up on the technology entirely—but he certainly speaks with the same echo as many industry skeptics, including (perhaps tellingly) Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick himself . items.title: Keychron K8 Ultra 8K review
items.summary: Solid, dependable and versatile.
items.body: Keychron has carved out a wonderful niche in the now admittedly overcrowded mechanical keyboard space for offering fantastic all-round keyboards with all the features and robustness you could want for a surprisingly affordable price, given what's on offer. The new K8 Ultra 8K might feel like I'm parroting a lot of the same thoughts as I have with the numerous other Keychron products I've tested simply because most products I've tested from them have been consistently excellent. This new model doesn't deviate from a lot of the established formula: hefty aluminium top case, PBT keycaps, versatile connectivity, web-based software. And let me tell you, that's no bad thing. Okay, against the likes of the Lemokey L4 and Keychron Q3 Max , I can nitpick and say the entire case isn't the usual machined aluminium as there's a doubleshot ABS portion on the underside mated to an aluminium top piece. items.title: AngryMiao AM Infinity.97 mouse review
items.summary: Flagship speed, boutique flair.
items.body: 2026 is shaping up to be an immense year for high-end gaming mice, with everything from the Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike to the Razer Viper V4 Pro and the Corsair Sabre V2 Pro proving genuine innovation, with everything from materials to speed and potency all covered off. So when the AngryMiao AM Infinity.97 came across my desk promising a sub-50 g weight with a 30,000 DPI sensor, 8000 Hz wireless polling and some very innovative battery tech, it definitely piqued my interest. AngryMiao is a brand I associate more with its keyboards than mice, with it having a penchant for the weird and wacky, opting for sci-fi-type designs in a similar vein to Gravastar. The AM Infinity.97 doesn't deviate from that formula, opting for a very holey chassis with an aggressive look all in the name of both lightness and standing out from a very crowded ultralight mouse market. It's purposefully been designed to be smaller than other mice to shed weight while keeping things comfortable, shaving three percent off a 'standard' size, hence the 97 in its name—it refers to being 97% of a full mouse. items.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker's final system requirements include upscaling set to Balanced—so unsurprisingly, they're lower
items.summary: Who would've thought?
items.body: Squinting at the new The Blood of Dawnwalker system requirements this morning before my second cup of coffee, my bleary eyes registered that the listed GPUs are often significantly less powerful than the previous recommended specs . As my tired eyeballs came into focus, though, it became clear why: upscaling, of course. Rebel Wolves has taken into account the modern inventions of DLSS, FSR, and XeSS in its final specs sheet. A reply to the X thread from the official account reveals that the new specs are based on Balanced upscaling settings , which would account for some of the drops. Why the Balanced setting wasn't clearly stated on the specs image and left for a thread reply to clear up is beyond me. Anyway, for 1080p 30 fps gameplay, Rebel Wolves now recommends an Intel Core i5 11400F or AMD Ryzen 7 2700X, alongside 16 GB of RAM and an Nvidia GTX 1060 or AMD Radeon RX 580 . items.title: Subnautica 2's latest 1.2 update is friend focused—finally adding the key mechanic to any great multiplayer game
items.summary: Nothing's impossible when you have the power of friendship.
items.body: I'm not sure there's been a better invention for multiplayer games than proximity chat. Whether it be friends screaming vengeance down the side of a mountain after you abandon them in Peak , or the wails of one of your fellow workers fall suspiciously silent in Lethal Company . Proximity chat offers up fertile ground for hilariously wacky and memorable multiplayer moments, so you can imagine my excitement when I found out it's coming to Subnautica 2 . "This is going to let you have an in-game voice chat option that you can do with your friends," Anthony Gallegos, creative director, says in a dev diary . "You'll be able to talk locally with each other and then as you get further away you'll hear a switch to sort of a radio-sounding voice, and you'll progressively break up as you get further away, up until a certain point where you can almost not hear me at all." Now, you can use your friends as a canary, sending them down into dark caves and listening to see if anything's amiss. items.title: Acer Predator Helios NEO 16S AI review
items.summary: A tale of two chippies as cursed power delivery strikes again.
items.body: I do love a good puzzle. There's something real satisfying about looking at the benchmark results and specs of two different laptops and coming to a crisp, neat conclusion on why one, that's so similar on paper, performs so differently to another. That's great and all, but the fact that that fact is even a thing is a problem. The fact that we're talking about that fact here right now, as a thing, with Acer's latest Predator Helios Neo is a problem. And it shouldn't be. Because you should be able to look at any laptop, see a GPU name, and know what performance you're getting, straight away. It shouldn't be ambiguous. You shouldn't have to dive into reviews, and you shouldn't need to go hunting around in the murky deep waters of spec manuals, trying to find out exactly if this new RTX 5080 is only as good as an RTX 5060, or secretly an RTX 5090 pretending to be an RTX 5070. items.title: Fired Rockstar workers say you shouldn't boycott GTA 6 for them: 'We spent years pouring our hard work, skill, and creativity into making GTA'
items.summary: "That doesn't mean we want you to let Rockstar off the hook."
items.body: Rockstar's been embroiled for some time in a legal dispute after firing 30 unionised workers in the UK , which has, naturally, been seen as union-busting behaviour by those impacted. The workers, who are part of The Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB), have been making solid progress. In June of this year, it was decided that IWGB would be allowed to present its case that Rockstar had allegedly blacklisted its unionised employees —as in, compiled a list of union members—which would be in violation of The Employment Relations Act , which plainly states that you can't compile a "details of persons who are or have been members of trade unions" for the purposes of "treating a person less favourably than another on grounds of trade union membership or trade union activities." The full trial will be held in September, but in the meantime, the IWGB has stated that folks excited for GTA 6 don't have to boycott the game on their behalf.
